chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the salt flats, so he said:

"And what is the salt flat?" I said: "It is a barren salty land in which water gathers and then becomes salt." He said: "It is like a mine; khums is due on it." I said: "Then sulfur and oil are extracted from the earth?" He said: "This and its like, khums is due on it."

key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: the one-fifth tax due on certain forms of wealth or extracted resources
key_terms.الْمَعْدِنِ: a mine or mineral source, used here as the legal analogy
key_terms.الْمَلَّاحَةُ: salt flat; saline land where water gathers and turns into salt
key_terms.مِلْحًا: salt produced from the collected water

ai.seo_question: Is khums required on salt, sulfur, oil, and other substances extracted from the earth?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that salt flats producing salt are treated like mineral resources, and khums is due on them. It also extends the same ruling to sulfur, oil, and similar substances extracted from the earth, showing a broader legal principle regarding extractive resources.
